---
title: "check-tree-lists.yml"
---

Diff-scoped, blocking check that flags a tree written only as a nested list.
The lab's rule (Ezra, 2026-10-26) is that a tree (a parse tree, decision tree,
dendrogram or any other hierarchy) is drawn as a diagram figure,
not only written as nested bullets.
This implements
[gha#1263](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1263).

A div is flagged when all of these hold:

- it is a definition, example, theorem-type, remark or exercise div
  (`#def-`, `#exm-`, `#thm-`, `#lem-`, `#cor-`, `#prp-`, `#rem-`, `#exr-`);
- its text mentions a tree ("tree", "trees" or "dendrogram");
- it holds a list nested three or more levels deep
  (three distinct indentation widths among its list items);
- it holds no figure: a Markdown image or `<img>` tag,
  a div or chunk labelled `fig-`, an `@fig-` cross-reference,
  or an include of a `_fig` subfile.

Keep the list too when it adds information, and add the figure beside it.
A justified exception carries a reason:
an HTML comment `<!-- no-tree-figure: reason -->` inside the div exempts it.
Use `paths-ignore` to exempt whole paths.

## Scope

Only a div that holds a line a pull request adds is reported,
so existing trees are never reflagged.
The whole file is parsed, since a div opens far above the changed line.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new, and a blank added line is not content.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed,
the check skips with a warning instead of scanning the whole tree.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file on purpose,
which measures how many existing trees are only lists.
Every run prints how many lines, files and divs it examined.

## Inputs

| Input          | Type    | Default       | Description |
| -------------- | ------- | ------------- | ----------- |
| `globs`        | string  | `'*.qmd'`     | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore` | string  | `''`          | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`         | boolean | `true`        | Fail the workflow when a tree is only a list. Set `false` for warning annotations only. |
| `whole-tree`   | boolean | `false`       | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string | `'3.x'`      | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | `'ubuntu-latest'` | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-tree-lists.yml in your repo.
# Diff-scoped check: flags a def/exm/thm/rem/exr div that mentions a tree and
# holds a list nested 3+ levels with no figure, when a PR adds a line to it.
# Add a figure, or <!-- no-tree-figure: reason --> in the div.
# Blocking by default.
# Only contents:read is needed (the default), so no permissions block is required.
name: Check tree lists

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-tree-lists.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   globs: '*.qmd'                        # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'chapters/outtakes/**'   # skip known-noisy paths
    #   fail: true                             # set false to warn only (defaults to true)
    #   whole-tree: true                       # scan every file, not just a PR's additions
```

See
[`examples/check-tree-lists.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-tree-lists.yml)
for the full caller stub.
